hypothesis: Who the household is (demographics) and when the snapshot is (calendar) predict 4-week spend.
transformation_description: Baseline: demographic codes, has_demographics, snapshot day index, week-of-year.

hypothesis: A household's recent purchasing behavior (spend rates over 28/56/84/168/364-day windows, trip counts, basket sizes, recency, trend) predicts its next-4-week spend far better than demographics alone.
transformation_description: Added behavioral history features: spend/trips/products/stores/qty per window (28,56,84,168,364,728d), avg/max basket size, active days, discounts, trend ratios, lag-1y spend, tenure, recency; kept demographics + calendar.
reasoning_summary: Raw past-spend blends already achieve ~66 MAE vs baseline 92.5; a gradient-boosted model over rich recency/trend features should capture this signal plus interactions.

hypothesis: What a household buys predicts future spend beyond how much it spent: department spend shares, private-brand share, discount reliance, marketing exposure (campaign targeting, coupon redemptions), and purchase cadence/volatility add predictive signal to E001's spend-rate history.
transformation_description: Added to E001: 7/14-day spend+trips, recency-weighted EWMA spend (half-lives 14/28/56d), department spend shares (84/364d), private-brand share, discount share, avg unit price, evening-purchase share, campaign targeting counts (A/B/C/active), coupon redemption counts/recency, inter-trip gap stats, weekly spend volatility.
reasoning_summary: Household-level mix and discount/marketing behavior characterize spending style; EWMA and cadence features capture recency and regularity that raw window sums miss, so they should sharpen spend forecasts.

hypothesis: Spend dynamics beyond raw window sums — momentum (recent minus half-window spend), ratios (recent/longer spend, trips, products), spend-per-trip/day, rising-spend interactions, store-loyalty share, weekly volatility, and seasonal lag — improve prediction of 4-week future spend over E002's raw aggregates.
transformation_description: Added to E001: 15 dynamics features (momentum m_sp28_56/m_sp56_84, ratios r_sp28_84/r_sp84_364/r_tr28_84/r_pr28_84, spt_84, spd_84, i_sp28_rise/i_sp84_rise, topstore, wkstd, wkmax, splag1y, nact14).
reasoning_summary: Two households with equal 84-day spend behave differently if spend is accelerating vs. decaying; ratios and momentum capture acceleration, per-trip/per-day intensity, concentration of spend at one store, and weekly variability that raw window sums miss.

hypothesis: Marketing exposure predicts future spend: campaign targeting (active/recent campaigns, type counts), coupon redemption history, and loyalty/discount reliance (share of spend paid with coupon/retail discounts) signal engagement and price sensitivity that carry into the next 4 weeks.
transformation_description: Added to E003: 24 marketing features — n_camp_targeted/active/recent, campaign-type counts, coupon redemption counts over 28/56/84/168d + recency + distinct campaigns, and coupon/retail/deal discount share of spend over 28/56/84d.
reasoning_summary: Campaign-targeted and coupon-redeeming households are more engaged; discount share captures deal-driven purchasing, which may persist into the next 4 weeks.

hypothesis: Intended: future 4-week spend is driven by trip cadence (expected trips = 28/median gap, × spend-per-trip) and household seasonality (same week-of-year spend one year earlier) — but the new feature table could not be built (isolated runner crashed at validation snapshots; build abandoned). Fallback: re-evaluation of the parent E003 table to keep a valid record; expected result equals E003 (MAE ≈ 60.72).
transformation_description: None — fallback re-evaluation of the parent E003 feature table (e003_full.parquet) after the intended cadence/seasonality feature build failed to save.
reasoning_summary: No new features could be constructed within the tool-call budget; re-evaluating the unchanged parent table preserves a valid experiment record and confirms E003's baseline of MAE 60.72.

hypothesis: Trip cadence (gap variability, expected trips = 28/median gap) and basket-size distribution (median/std/max, expected spend = trips × mean basket) predict future 4-week spend; day-of-week trip regularity and seasonal same-window spend add signal.
transformation_description: Added to E003: 30 cadence/basket features — gap std/CV, expected trips, expected spend, basket-value med/std/max, no-trip-28 flag, trip weekday-residue mix, seasonal 4-week spend/trips and ratio, evening share.
reasoning_summary: Future spend ≈ (expected trips in next 28d) × (typical basket value); gap regularity and basket dispersion should sharpen that estimate beyond E003's window sums, and weekday regularity captures habitual shopping patterns.

hypothesis: Temporal structure beyond trailing windows predicts future spend: lag-aligned 4-week windows (spend/trips at lag 2, 3 and same-window one/two years ago), log-transformed trailing spend, tenure/recency, and promotion-engagement (coupon/loyalty discount totals and discount share of spend).
transformation_description: Added to E003: 22 temporal features — n7_sp_/n7_tr_ for lag2 (28-56d), lag3 (56-84d), seas1y (364-392d), seas2y (728-756d); log1p of 28/84/364d spend; tenure, recency, had_hist_1y; coupon/retail/match discount totals and discount share over 28d and 84d.
reasoning_summary: The 28-day-ahead target is autocorrelated at its own horizon, so the spend 28-56 days ago and the same calendar window a year ago should add signal the trailing-window features miss; promotion engagement captures short-lived demand shifts.

hypothesis: Future 4-week spend is best predicted by the household's robust long-run spend level (median of aligned 4-week windows), its lapse/zero-rate pattern, and its recent weekly trajectory — heavy-tailed targets are better captured with log1p window sums and level/shape features than with raw means.
transformation_description: Added to E003: 28 level/shape features — log1p window sums (28/56/84/168/364d), weekly spend trajectory (12 lags), weekly CV and active-week share, tenure/recency, mean weekly spend over tenure, last-3-day spend, and aligned-4w-window median/max/zero-rate/count over full history.
reasoning_summary: Target is heavy-tailed with a 20% zero mass; robust level (median 4w window), lapse rate and log-compressed recent trajectory should capture the level and intermittency that raw window means miss.

hypothesis: A household's own past 4-week outcomes are the strongest predictor of its next 4-week spend: target encoding of prior train-window outcomes (mean/median/std/min/max, count, last-3 average, day-slope) gives the model a direct, low-noise estimate of the household's spend level and trend, beyond the transaction-derived features of E008.
transformation_description: Added to E008: 8 leave-time-safe target-encoding features computed from train targets only (per-household mean/median/std/min/max/count of past future_spend_4w, mean of last 3 outcomes, and slope over snapshot_day).
reasoning_summary: te_mean correlates 0.866 with the train target — far above any transaction feature — and for validation snapshots it is a strictly backward-looking household spend level/trend, so it should sharpen predictions where E008's behavioral proxies are noisy.

hypothesis: Future 4-week spend is better predicted by the household's gross (pre-discount) demand than by net spend alone: net = gross × (1 − deal share), so gross-spend windows, gross/net ratios, gross EWMA and gross momentum recover the demand signal that discounts obscure.
transformation_description: Added to E008: 15 gross-spend features — log1p gross spend over 28/56/84/168/364d windows (gross = sales_value − retail_disc − coupon_disc − coupon_match_disc), gross/net spend ratios over 28/84/364d, gross EWMA (half-lives 28/56d), gross momentum (log gross 28d − log gross 84d), seasonal gross (same 4w last year), and net−gross log gap over 364d.
reasoning_summary: E008 only saw net spend; decomposing into gross demand and deal share gives the model the pre-discount level that drives future purchases, plus a cleaner deal-intensity measure than the 364d-only discshare.

error: exceeded 15 tool calls without calling the evaluation tool

hypothesis: Beyond E008's trailing-window spend levels, three new signal families predict future 4-week spend: (1) global seasonal/trend context (per-week retailer-wide spend per active household, relative to the same weeks a year earlier) shifts every household's next-4-week spend; (2) stock-up basket shape (max/median basket, days since biggest basket, big-basket count and spend share) flags households whose recent spend is inflated by a stock-up that will not repeat; (3) time-of-day mix of spend marks households with different trip purposes. Local GBM CV on E008 features: 70.19 -> 69.93/69.95/69.96 for the three groups individually; combined table tested here.
transformation_description: Added to E008: 15 new features — global weekly spend-per-active-household level/trend/seasonal (4 scalars), 6 stock-up/basket-shape features, 3 time-of-day features, plus 2 share features kept from the habit group (repeat and new-product shares). Parent: E008.
reasoning_summary: Seasonal context, stock-up cycles and trip-purpose mix carry information orthogonal to trailing window sums, and each group improved local CV over E008.

hypothesis: Complementary disjoint feature families are additive: E008's level/shape features plus E006's cadence/basket features plus E007's lag-aligned seasonal features jointly predict future 4-week spend better than E008 alone (each family matched E003 within noise with disjoint information).
transformation_description: Merged E008 with E006 (30 cadence/basket features) and E007 (22 lag-aligned temporal features): union of all three sibling tables, 217 features total.
reasoning_summary: E006/E007/E012 each tied E003 within noise with non-overlapping signals; combining them gives the model complementary information (trip cadence, seasonal lags, momentum) that a single family misses, so MAE should drop below 60.697.

hypothesis: A small, high-signal subset of E008's features beats the full 163-feature set under the harness model: long-horizon spend levels (sp364, sp728), their rate (sp364_rate), breadth (prods728, nact728, trips728, nact364, trips364), discount magnitude (rdisc364) and basket-shape (z_max4w_hist) capture the durable spend level without noise.
transformation_description: Kept only 10 of E008's columns (sp728, sp364, sp364_rate, prods728, nact728, rdisc364, nact364, trips728, trips364, z_max4w_hist); dropped the other 153 features.
reasoning_summary: Local ridge probes on later train snapshots show the 10-feature long-horizon set reaching ~100 MAE vs ~140 for the full set, suggesting E008's wide feature set adds noise for the harness model; pruning to the strongest predictors may improve validation MAE.

hypothesis: Exposure to in-store displays and weekly mailers for the products a household actually buys predicts its future 4-week spend beyond trailing spend levels: promo-active purchasing (share of spend on displayed/mailer'd items and commodities, 28/84d) captures forward-looking demand stimulus and store engagement that trailing windows miss; a snapshot-drift term adds level correction.
transformation_description: Added to E008: 10 features — pm_share84/28, pc_share84/28 (commodity-week promo exposure), pdisp_share84, pmail_share84, pm_spend84/28, p_wks84 (promo-active weeks), snap_idx (drift). Built via item-store-week and commodity-week joins to display_mailer promo flags.
reasoning_summary: display_mailer is the only untapped table; my offline ridge proxy shows +0.7 MAE improvement (63.77→63.07), the largest of any candidate family tested, so the exposure signal should transfer to the harness model.

hypothesis: A household's own realized past 4-week outcomes on the same 28-day grid (last ~10 disjoint 4-week spend windows, recency-decayed/shrunk summaries) are the strongest safe predictor of its next 4-week spend; overlapping trailing windows blur the zero/churn pattern that grid-aligned windows expose directly.
transformation_description: Added to E008: 43 grid-aligned features — 14 disjoint 4-week spend windows (log1p, bucket 0 = [s−27,s]), 6 trip-count windows, per-window mean/median/std/min/max, zero-window share, OLS slope over valid windows, EWMA (halflife 6/85 windows), shrinkage means toward global mean, log-ratios (recent vs 2–8w, w0 vs 1y seasonal), days-since-last-purchase decay.
reasoning_summary: Grid-aligned windows exactly match the target's time structure, so they directly expose churn/zero patterns and seasonality that overlapping trailing windows average away; raw correlations (0.79–0.82) far exceed E008's typical features.

hypothesis: The four complementary, individually-validated feature families — robust long-run spend level/shape (E008), trip cadence and basket-size distributions (E006), lag-aligned seasonal temporal windows (E007), and grid-aligned disjoint past 4-week spend windows (E016) — are jointly informative: their grand union gives the fixed linear model the fullest leak-free picture of a household's spend process and matches or beats E008 (60.697) on validation MAE.
transformation_description: Relative to E013 (E008+E006+E007 union, 215 features), added the 41 grid-aligned disjoint 4-week window features from E016 (g_lw0..13, g_w*, g_ew*, g_shr*, g_dlog*, g_lt*, g_tmean/g_tzero/g_dsl/g_expact/g_dlog_seas), deduplicated overlapping columns, for 256 total features.
reasoning_summary: A late-train holdout screen (fit on snapshots 95-375, evaluate 403/431) showed the grand union at MAE 63.50 vs 63.63 for E008 alone, and E013 already matched E008 on the harness; the disjoint grid-window family adds past-outcome structure the trailing windows miss.

hypothesis: The harness regression is effectively linear in the features, so concave transforms (sqrt/log) of heavy-tailed spend levels, empirical-Bayes-shrunk expected next-4w spend (rate shrunk to the global daily rate), and level-x-cadence interactions of the top signals capture curvature that raw levels miss and reduce validation MAE below E013's 60.70.
transformation_description: Added to E013: 28 non-linear/interaction features — sqrt and log1p transforms of 8 top level features (sp28/sp84/sp364, rates, wksp_mean, z_med4w_hist, z_mean_week_spend_all), EB-shrunk expected 4w spend at 84/168/364d windows, zero-rate-adjusted expectations, 6 level-x-cadence/recency interaction products, and a weighted level blend.
reasoning_summary: All feature families plateaued at ~60.7, suggesting the fixed model is linear and saturating on raw levels; concave transforms and interactions add curvature that raw sums cannot express, and EB shrinkage gives a better-calibrated level estimate for sparse households.

hypothesis: The disjoint 4-week grid windows' shape statistics (weighted recency-weighted sums, EWMA, level/median/std/slope/zero-rate, log-diff autocorrelation, and trip-timing summaries) carry predictive signal complementary to E013's level/cadence/lag families; adding the 26 most informative grid-shape features (excluding the 14 raw lagged window levels g_lw*, which E016 showed add noise) to the E013 union improves validation MAE below E013's 60.703.
transformation_description: Merged E013 union (E008 level/shape + E006 cadence/basket + E007 lag-aligned temporal, 215 features) with 26 grid-shape features from E016's table (g_w0r/w1r/w2r, g_wmean/wmed/wstd/wmin/wmax/wzero/wslope, g_ew6/ew85, g_shr1/shr3, g_dlog_01/dlog_rm/dlog_seas, g_lt0..lt5, g_tmean/tzero, g_dsl, g_expact), dropping the 14 raw disjoint-window levels g_lw* that E016 showed hurt. 242 features total.
reasoning_summary: E016's grid windows helped only as a standalone family; its raw window levels added noise on top of E013, but the shape statistics (recency-weighted sums, EWMA, variability, slope, autocorrelation) summarize the same history more compactly and should add signal without the noise.
